Case_18015/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1: Photograph of the distal right lower extremity skin lesion

description.short_caption: Photograph of a distal right lower extremity skin lesion with central necrosis and surrounding erythema.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a skin lesion on the distal right lower extremity. The lesion has a central area of necrosis with dark eschar, surrounded by erythema and scaling. The surrounding skin appears inflamed, with desquamation extending outward. A suture is visible near the lesion, suggesting prior intervention or biopsy. The lesion's appearance is consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process.

Case_18015/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: Photograph of the distal left lower extremity skin lesion

description.short_caption: Photograph of a skin lesion on the distal left lower extremity.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a localized skin lesion on the distal left lower extremity. The lesion is characterized by a central necrotic area with black eschar, surrounded by an erythematous and indurated zone. The surrounding skin appears mildly swollen, and there is evidence of inflammation. The lesion's features suggest a possible infectious or necrotizing process.
visible_findings: central necrotic area with black eschar

Case_18015/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3: GMS stain of skin biopsy showed fungal elements/hyphae in areas of necrosis. These hyphae were focally twisted and ribbon-like, with only rare septae formation (100x oil immersion magnification)

description.short_caption: GMS stain of skin biopsy showing fungal hyphae in necrotic tissue.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a GMS (Gomori methenamine silver) stain of a skin biopsy under high magnification (100x oil immersion). The fungal elements are prominently stained black against a green background. The hyphae appear ribbon-like, with occasional twisting and rare septation, consistent with fungal morphology. The surrounding tissue shows areas of necrosis, further highlighting the fungal invasion.

Case_18015/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Figure 4: Fine white hyphae growth seen on Sabouraud-dextrose agar plate (day 3 of culture).

description.short_caption: White hyphal growth on Sabouraud-dextrose agar plate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Sabouraud-dextrose agar plate with fine, white, filamentous fungal growth consistent with hyphae. The growth radiates outward from two central inoculation points, forming a dense, fuzzy appearance. The colonies are surrounded by a lighter, diffuse zone of growth. The plate is being held in a gloved hand, suggesting a sterile handling environment.

Case_18015/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Figure 5: GMS stain of repeat skin debridement showed abundant ribbon-like hyphae with rare septae (40x magnification)

description.short_caption: GMS stain showing abundant ribbon-like hyphae with rare septae.
description.detailed_description: This is a Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stain of a skin specimen obtained during repeat debridement. The image shows abundant ribbon-like fungal hyphae with rare septations, consistent with a fungal infection. The hyphae are stained black against a green background, characteristic of GMS staining. The magnification appears to be approximately 40x.
